summary: This resolution sets the rules for House debate on H.R. 8035 by waiving all points of order, treating the bill as read, limiting debate to one hour split between the Judiciary and Intelligence committees, and allowing one motion to recommit before a final vote.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a purely procedural measure governing House consideration of H.R. 8035. It contains no appropriations, authorizations, or other provisions affecting federal outlays.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the resolution text.
The resolution addresses only floor procedure for a FISA-extension bill and has no connection to health policy or coverage.
No references to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The measure is silent on immigration, border policy, or related legal pathways.
No content touching reproductive rights or abortion access.
While FISA authorities support national-security collection, the resolution itself neither authorizes nor appropriates defense funds and does not alter military spending levels.
No environmental or regulatory provisions are present.
The resolution does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social spending.
No education policy, funding, or school-choice language exists.
No drug-enforcement or decriminalization provisions.
The underlying FISA bill concerns foreign-intelligence surveillance rather than domestic criminal sentencing or policing reforms; the resolution itself is procedural only.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures.
No deficit, debt-ceiling, or fiscal-policy language.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
The resolution does not address foreign assistance or aid programs.
No election-administration, voting-access, or campaign-finance content.

Although the bill being considered (H.R. 8035) extends FISA surveillance authorities that implicate privacy, the resolution itself is strictly procedural and contains no substantive surveillance or data-protection language.
No labor, union, or workplace-regulation provisions.
No religious-exemption or anti-discrimination measures.
